cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The house is migrating south. Help me redirect it before we lose the driveway. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The surveyor says subsidence. He's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Concrete traps it halfway across the road. Tell him we're planning a route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. It needs a guide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house is migrating south. Help me redirect it before we lose the driveway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The surveyor says subsidence. He's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concrete traps it halfway across the road. Tell him we're planning a route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. It needs a guide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then water isn't its grievance. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Give it my chair. A seat at the table should get us tea.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a biscuit instead. If one comes out, we won't need your tongue as equipment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a biscuit instead. If one comes out, we won't need your tongue as equipment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's an invisible bridge across this ditch. Tap for it with your umbrella before I cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use your walking stick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yours extends. You can test it without leaving the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probe. But a surface isn't proof it'll hold you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slide your picnic basket onto it first. Leave my lunch inside; I want a convincing weight.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I drew that floating staircase last week. Mention the date. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I drew the handrail while you called it nonsense.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Well done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loud enough for the people using my prediction to get upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew that floating staircase last week. Mention the date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew the handrail while you called it nonsense.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Well done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loud enough for the people using my prediction to get upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believed the cupboard before it learned to speak.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking for silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One quick acknowledgment, then I'll respect its wishes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says you talk too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An informed opinion formed over years of my support.

cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before we move the sofa: are we shrinking while the room stays normal, or is the room growing while we stay normal? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever gets this move finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Shrinking means call full-sized help. Growing means hurry before the door gets farther away. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to bring tweezers. He'll need to collect us afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we move the sofa: are we shrinking while the room stays normal, or is the room growing while we stay normal?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever gets this move finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shrinking means call full-sized help. Growing means hurry before the door gets farther away. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to bring tweezers. He'll need to collect us afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sandwiches are floating. Is gravity late for lunch, or has it resigned? We need a serving plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The guests arrive in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Late means plates underneath. Resigned means string on every sandwich. Which are we doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Late. We haven't enough string.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then fetch the deep plates. We may get the whole buffet at once.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The ceiling's hungry. Turn the breakfast tray upside down so it can eat. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last porridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Keep half for us. Just turn its bowl over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch anything it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Hold it under the light fitting; that's where it dribbled yesterday.

beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's hungry. Turn the breakfast tray upside down so it can eat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last porridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep half for us. Just turn its bowl over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch anything it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Hold it under the light fitting; that's where it dribbled yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Reserve two chairs for her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only saved her one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.
